text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Political leaders are very uptight amid Islamist-secularist arguments and recurrent speculation the army may move to oust the Islamist-conservative government.
- Workers and artisans are cooperating in their protest against the Islamist-led government's moves to introduce Islamist norms into public life.
- Everyone is focusing on a meeting of the powerful national security council on Friday. The council is expected to discuss the latest strains between Islamists and secularists.
- Two MPs resigned from the Democratic Left Party of former prime minister Bulent Ecevit. Deputy premier Tansu Ciller says the pair will join her conservative party.
- Former head of the state social security institution says there are 32 ways of evading tax in Turkey.
- Defence minister Turhan Tayan says Iran supports Kurdish separatist guerrillas in Turkey.
- Turkish industrists group is planning to increase its role in central and eastern Turkey.
- Parliament rejects censure motion against the government.
